Late Shifts

Maya, 22, moves back to her hometown after dropping out of grad school. She takes the night shift at Mel's, a 24-hour diner two blocks from her brother's apartment. The diner owner notices everything. The cook on her shift barely speaks. The head waitress teaches her the floor. Her older brother is quietly there when she comes home at dawn. The neighbor in 2B has thin walls and a long memory.

body_text:
His mug is rinsed and upside down in the rack the way he always leaves it. The burner he used is still warm when she sets the back of her hand against it. Six-forty, maybe. She'd lost the habit of knowing what time it was.

The window above the sink looks out at the parking lot and, past it, a diner sign two blocks down with one dead letter. MEL'S. She'd noticed it when they drove in from the bus station with her three bags. She hadn't gone in yet.

Look at the sign.
